csv_project_name: AE for CSU Athletics Complex Renovations & Additions
csv_scope_of_work: Cleveland State University (CSU) is seeking architectural/engineering services for renovations and additions to the Physical Education (PE) Building to house intercollegiate athletics, academics, and administration. This project will transform Woodling Gymnasium to serve as the main competition venue for men s and women s basketball and volleyball. A new addition will also be added adjacent to Woodling Gym and/or the PE Building to house dedicated practice facilities for men s and women s basketball. In addition, a volleyball practice facility will need to be identified. The selected firm will be responsible for studying the athletic facilities listed below and developing a Program of Requirements (POR) as a part of this project. owing facilities are the areas under consideration for this project: Physical Education Building o Woodling Gymnasium o Sub-Basement Level o Basement Level o Court Level o Mezzanine Level All surrounding areas adjacent to the Physical Education Building, including but not limited to: o The southwest PE lawn o Those areas abutting the Recreation Center o The western lobbies outside Woodling Gym o The eastern driveway and alley outside Woodling Gym o The space south of Woodling Gym
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Interior Design/Space Planning, Rehabilitation & Refurbishment, Civil Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping, Cost Estimating, Feasibility Studies, Electrical Engineering, Fire Protection Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering

title: A/E Services for CSU Athletics Complex Renovations and Additions
short_description: Renovation and expansion of Cleveland State University's athletics complex and Woodling Gymnasium.
project_scope: Renovation and additions to the Cleveland State University Physical Education Building to accommodate intercollegiate athletics, academics, and administration. The project will transform Woodling Gymnasium into the main competition venue for men's and women's basketball and volleyball. A new addition adjacent to Woodling Gym and/or the PE Building will provide dedicated practice facilities for men's and women's basketball, and a volleyball practice facility must also be identified. Areas under consideration include Woodling Gymnasium, sub-basement, basement, court level, mezzanine level, and surrounding exterior areas such as the southwest PE lawn, areas abutting the Recreation Center, western lobbies outside Woodling Gym, the eastern driveway and alley, and space south of Woodling Gym.
services: Architectural and engineering services including architecture, interior design/space planning, rehabilitation and refurbishment, civil engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, cost estimating, feasibility studies, electrical engineering, fire protection engineering, mechanical engineering, and structural engineering; development of a Program of Requirements (POR).
relevance_explanation:
- Large public university athletics renovation and expansion project.
- Includes structural engineering within a multidisciplinary A/E scope.
- Sports facilities are generally relevant to sbp, especially competition and practice venues.
- Existing-building renovation plus additions may involve complex structural interventions.
- However, the procurement is broad A/E-led and not specifically focused on a standout long-span or signature structural concept.
construction_cost_explanation: Estimated from the tender documents, which state a total construction cost range of $30.0M-$60.0M; midpoint used: $45.0M.
fee_explanation: No explicit design fee stated in the source. Useful basis: total construction cost is given as $30.0M-$60.0M for a multidisciplinary A/E assignment including architecture and engineering services.
references_qualifications: Multidisciplinary A/E capability is implied, including architecture, interior design/space planning, rehabilitation and refurbishment, civil engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, cost estimating, feasibility studies, electrical, fire protection, mechanical, and structural engineering.
